summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Atlas Retail through the Console tracing UI: request logs, error analysis, and debugging flows. Customer is primarily concerned about slow tail latency for inference, auditability (SOC2/SSO), and the ability to correlate trace IDs to raw request logs for POC benchmarking. Agreed next steps: send security pack, share traces, and schedule a 1-week POC starting 2026-11-22.
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-09 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (Atlas CTO), Priya Singh (SRE Lead), Marta Lopez (Security)
Shared: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/console-tracing, sample traces sheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/atlas-sample

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, request logs, and debugging slow responses / error patterns.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we'll walk through the Console tracing and request-logs flows. Daniel's going to drive the demo and I'll jump in on commercial / next steps.
[00:22] Daniel: cool, so opening the Console \u001F top left you'll see "Tracing". We capture per-request trace IDs, stages like routing, KV-cache, model-infer, and token writeback. You can filter by model, route, and customer id.
[00:45] Jared: quick Q \u001F can we map trace IDs back to our internal correlation id? we send x-correlation-id in header.
[00:57] Daniel: yes, you can ingest any header as a tag; in the UI search I can type correlation-id: 1234 and it pulls the exact request, we also show the full request log on the right pane.
[01:18] Priya: is the request log raw? like does it contain prompt text? we need to be careful for PII.
[01:28] Daniel: by default request logs include minimal metadata; customers can opt-in for full request bodies for POC only. We also have on/off toggles and retention controls; everything is encrypted at rest with KMS.
[01:44] Marta: do you have audit logs for who viewed a trace? that's critical for us.
[01:51] Maya: yes, Console has an audit trail, SSO + RBAC integration \u001F we support SAML/Okta and SCIM. We can include audit exports for compliance teams.
[02:05] Daniel: back to the trace view \u001F here you can see spans: routing decision (host selection), batching, KV cache hit/miss (sometimes transcribed as K V cash in logs), model execution time, and post-processing. You can expand spans to see GPU task durations and approximate token counts.
[02:34] [screen share glitch] Speaker 1: oh sorry the screen share dropped, re-sharing.
[02:48] Daniel: no worries \u001F reloading the trace. Here's an example trace-id: ff-trace-20261109-7b1e, we see a spike at the model-infer span, p95 is 780ms for this model.
[03:10] Priya: our problem is tail latency \u001F we see occasional 2s+ for some routes. can you show how you'd debug that with request logs?
[03:22] Daniel: sure, click the "Errors & Latency" tab, then set filter latency>1000. It will surface request logs and associated traces. you can pivot by model, region, or instance. If it's batching, you'll see group sizes and wait times in span metadata.
[03:45] Jared: do you surface per-instance GPU metrics? e.g., GPU utilization on the node that served that request?
[03:53] Daniel: we do. the trace attaches host metrics snapshot (gpu%/mem) at the time of the span. For Dedicated customers we enrich traces with instance tags; for Hosted we provide sampled host metrics.
[04:10] Priya: can I export these logs into our SIEM?
[04:15] Daniel: yes, we have a request-logs export endpoint and S3/CloudWatch sinks. We can push to your Splunk/Datadog too.
[04:27] Marta: security question \u001F where are logs stored? region/retention?
[04:31] Maya: logs can be kept in-region, retention configurable per account; for Private deployments you control storage entirely. We support encryption with customer-managed KMS.
[04:44] Daniel: showing the "Error analysis" UI: it clusters error types \u001F model timeouts, invalid inputs, rate-limit rejections, and internal infra errors. you can click a cluster to see sample traces and the raw request.
[05:05] [crosstalk] Jared: do you have a way to re-run a request against a different model variant for debugging?
[05:12] Daniel: yes, we have a replay feature in the Console where you can re-run the exact payload against a pinned model or a local canary. note: replays are sandboxed and logged.
[05:28] Priya: how do you handle PII for replays? we cannot re-run pii-containing prompts outside certain controls.
[05:34] Daniel: replays respect redaction settings; we can mask prompts or use synthetic placeholders. For the POC we can enable masked replays and work with your security team.
[05:50] [00:06:00 approx] Daniel: switching to request logs \u001F here's a table view with each request row: timestamp, trace id, model, latency, status, route, correlation id. you can drill into a row to expand full JSON.
[06:15] Priya: the table's nice, can we get API access to query it programmatically?
[06:20] Daniel: yes, request-logs API gives you structured JSON and supports query params for time ranges and filters. we'll share a curl snippet after.
[06:31] Jared: for the POC we want to measure cost vs. latency tradeoffs \u001F can Console show aggregations like cost per-route?
[06:39] Maya: Cost dashboards will show token-based cost by route/model and we can correlate to latency buckets. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations (batch size, quantization) but for this demo we can surface per-route cost.
[06:56] Daniel: showing a live example, you can group by route and then stack latency percentiles and cost. you can export CSV for billing reconciliation.
[07:12] [07:30] Priya: one more on tracing \u001F what about KV cache? sometimes we suspect cache misses cause the tail.
[07:38] Daniel: we log cache hit/miss per request span; if misses happen you see the miss span and an upstream fetch. you can correlate sequence length and whether the request used cached prefix.
[07:50] Marta: compliance \u001F do you retain who accessed traces and when?
[07:55] Maya: yes audit logs capture UI actions and API tokens; we can provide logs for audits.
[08:03] [08:20] Daniel: let's demo a debugging flow end-to-end: filter for latency>1500ms, open the trace, identify stage with longest duration, check host metrics, then look at request payload and recent model version. often you can see an older model variant or a larger sequence length causing the spike.
[08:42] Jared: do you auto-suggest fixes? like suggest turning on prefix caching or smaller batch windows?
[08:48] Daniel: Redwood Optimize has rule recommendations; Console shows inline suggestions for batching and cache policies tied to the route. those are prescriptive but not auto-applied.
[09:03] Priya: how many traces do you retain by default?
[09:07] Daniel: default 30 days for hosted, customizable up to 365 for enterprise. Dedicated/Private options vary.
[09:18] Marta: can we get a redacted export for security review?
[09:21] Maya: absolutely, Daniel will prepare a redacted trace bundle.
[09:26] [10:00] Daniel: demo note \u001F occasional transcription typo: KVcache sometimes appears as K V cache in older logs; just ignore that if you search.
[10:34] Jared: on SLAs \u001F what are the latency SLO guarantees?
[10:38] Maya: for Hosted APIs we publish typical p50/p95 ranges per model; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency targets. We can include the SLA language in the POC contract.
[10:50] Priya: for the POC we'd like two things: 1) a week of traced traffic to verify tail behavior, 2) a small dedicated capacity for critical routes to test impact.
[11:02] Maya: sounds reasonable \u001F we can provision a short Dedicated reservation for the POC or use dedicated routing policies on hosted. we'll put both options in the follow-up.
[11:12] Jared: what about cost \u001F we need a ballpark for the week-run.
[11:17] Maya: I'll send a POC pricing sheet (estimates) and include assumptions on throughput and model selection.
[11:24] [12:00 approx] Daniel: quick technical aside: traces include model-infer token timing but not per-kernel metrics unless you run Dedicated with deeper profiling \u001F that is available for enterprise customers.
[12:40] Priya: okay can you also show how to correlate an internal error code to a model-level error?
[12:45] Daniel: yes, error clusters map internal infra codes to root causes, and you can click a sample to see the stack and the raw exception. we also surface rate-limit windows.
[13:03] Marta: for compliance we need the ability to redact specific fields in exported traces.
[13:09] Daniel: redaction rules are supported; we can set them at ingestion time.
[13:20] [13:45] Maya: recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2 & security pack, Daniel will export a few redacted traces and a sample request-log CSV, and we agreed to start a POC the week of 2026-11-22.
[14:05] Jared: thanks, that works.
[14:12] Priya: thanks all.
[14:18] Maya: I'll follow up with calendar invite and action-item list.

End transcript.

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-attributions and minor typos as typical for automated transcription.
file_notes: Demo focused on Console: tracing, request logs, error analysis, replay. AE+SE present. Customer is concerned with tail latency, audit logs, redaction and POC metrics.
